subject: BlueRidge performance qualification & pilot proposal
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@blueridge.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Jun 2028 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Performance discovery recap: latency, throughput, streaming needs

Hi Liam —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap so we have alignment and some clear next steps to qualify BlueRidge's performance requirements and propose a concrete pilot. I tried to capture the key constraints you shared; please correct anything that’s off.

Summary of requirements from call:
- Latency targets: p95 first-byte target ~120–180ms (you said lower is ideal for interactive UI). End-to-end for longer generative responses acceptable up to ~600ms for long sequences.
- Streaming: yes — incremental token streaming is required for the chat surface. You called out ~50–100ms per-token interactivity expectation for the UI.
- Throughput / concurrency: sustained ~700–800 requests/sec with ~1.8–2k concurrent open sessions during peak.
- Typical prompt lengths: median ~40–80 tokens, tail up to 1,024 tokens.
- Quality constraints: you want no more than a small regression vs current model; procurement will evaluate quality delta.

Primary pilot objective:
- Demonstrate p95 latency within the interactive target for the 90% of traffic that is short (<=128 tokens) while sustaining your 700–800 qps peak using Redwood’s streaming + batching stack.

Data we need from you to finalize pilot sizing/policy: (can you send these items?)
1) Traffic histogram (per-minute qps over 24 hrs) and payload size distribution (sample CSV is fine).
2) A couple of representative prompt+response pairs (to sanity-check caching/prefix-hit expectations).
3) Any hard compliance constraints (no model quantization allowed? specific KMS/HSM requirements?).

Immediate next steps I propose:
- You share the traffic histogram + sample prompts (attachment preferred).
- Redwood SE (Marcus) will put together two pilot configs: (A) latency-first (more capacity, conservative quantization) and (B) cost-optimized (aggressive batching + quantization fallback).
- 45-min kickoff next week to align on SLA, telemetry hooks, and dates.

I attached a short template (latency-profiles.csv) for the traffic histogram — feel free to populate or send your raw export.

Thanks —
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 20 Jun 2028 09:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Performance discovery recap: latency, throughput, streaming needs

Thanks Stephanie — appreciate the concise recap. A few clarifications and I’ve attached the traffic export + our SLO doc.

Clarifications from our infra/ops side:
- p95 first-byte: target is 180ms or better for the bulk of short responses (we used 120ms as a stretch target in the call).
- End-to-end (long responses): up to ~600ms is acceptable for responses that are >512 tokens.
- Streaming: required. The UI expects token-by-token arrivals; per-token latency should be under ~60ms in steady state.
- Peak numbers: sustained 700 qps for ~90 minutes during business hours; concurrent open websockets ~2k.
- We have a strong preference to avoid any quantization path that visibly degrades customer-facing quality, but for background inference (batch ranking) we can accept more aggressive quantization.

Attached: blueridge_traffic_histogram.csv, blueridge_slo_requirements_v1.pdf

Procurement (procurement@blueridge.ai) is on the thread — they’re interested in the pilot commercial terms (credits, trial duration). Ops is ops@blueridge.ai for any infra-level questions.

Liam O'Connor
Head of Product, BlueRidge AI

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 Jun 2028 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Performance discovery recap: latency, throughput, streaming needs

Stephanie / Neha —

I've sketched two pilot configurations and the cost/perf levers we should validate with BlueRidge. High-level notes below; I’ll attach a compact pilot-config-draft.yaml with the full knobs.

Pilot A — Latency-first (conservative):
- Serving: dedicated pool of low-latency GPUs (bfloat16 where available).
- Batching: continuous batching enabled, target max batch size 48, batch window 10–12ms to keep p95 low.
- Caching: prefix caching for repeated prompt prefixes (expected hit rate 60–75% based on their sample), TTL short (60s) to balance freshness.
- Quantization: none on primary path; use int8 only for background ranking traffic.
- Model variant: gptx-low-latency (smaller variant) for interactive path; gptx-standard for higher-quality background tasks.
- Expected: meet p95 first-byte <= 180ms for <=128 token responses; higher cost (rough estimate: $X per 1M tokens — see attached).

Pilot B — Cost-optimized (trade quality for cost):
- Serving: mixed instance types; autoscale to leverage higher throughput instances during tails.
- Batching: larger max batch size (96), batch window 20–30ms for better amortization.
- Caching: same prefix caching; add KV cache for repeated context across sessions.
- Quantization profile: dynamic int8 (safe profile) for ~70% of traffic with fallback to fp16 on QA failures — expected cost reduction ~25–35% with ~1–3% quality delta on measured evals.
- Model variant: gptx-standard with optional quantized variant for best-effort requests.

Operational controls we should include in the pilot:
- Auto-fallback policy: when p95 or error rate spikes, route a percentage of traffic to the low-latency variant or increase replicas.
- Observability: token-level latency breakdown, per-route cost, sampling of outputs for quality regression.
- SLA target to trial: p95 <= 180ms for interactive bucket; we can agree measurement windows.

Next asks for BlueRidge to finalize pilot sizing:
1) Confirmation on allowed quantization profiles (explicit opt-in per workload).
2) Sign-off on pilot window (we recommend 2 weeks of warm traffic after a 48-72h soak).
3) API key + telemetry hooks (we’ll give an ingestion endpoint for traces).

I attached pilot-config-draft.yaml and a quick cost estimate table (ballpark). Happy to turn this into a one-page SOW for procurement if Steph wants.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin

Subject: BlueRidge pilot proposal and next steps (45-min kickoff)

Hi Liam / Procurement —

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the histogram and SLO doc — that was super helpful. Marcus and I reviewed and proposed two pilot flavors (latency-first and cost-optimized). High-level pilot plan and asks:

Pilot scope:
- 2-week pilot (48–72h soak + 2 full business days of peak testing, then 10 days of steady validation).
- Telemetry: token-level latencies, p50/p95/p99, error rate, per-route cost; Redwood will provide a dashboard and a sampling stream of outputs for BlueRidge QA.
- Controls: we’ll run with conservative autoscaling rules and a live fallback to low-latency variant if p95 breaches agreed thresholds.

Commercials / procurement:
- For pilot we offer a credits package to cover the dedicated capacity and SE time; if procurement agrees we’ll send a short SOW and a DocuSign link.
- Procurement contact — can you confirm the correct PO contact and whether a short SOW is sufficient for sign-off?

Action items / timeline:
1) BlueRidge: confirm quantization opt-in per workload and PO contact (reply to this thread).
2) Redwood: finalize pilot-config-draft.yaml and SOW; provide kickoff slots (we have availability next Tue/Wed 10–2 PT).
3) Kickoff call (45 min) to align on telemetry hooks and cutover plan.

If that looks good I’ll send the DocuSign for the pilot SOW and drop proposed calendar invites.

Cheers —
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
